conviction_note: Company-level card credit (July 4.12%, Aug 4.16% domestic card NCO, Sept trust NCO 1.69%) points to a Q3 card NCO near 4.1-4.2% against 4.71% in Q2, so I expect the number to beat on provision (print_vs_bar +3% on adjusted EPS). But the monthly data is public, COF sold its last three prints including a Q2 adjusted-EPS beat (-2.36%), and Synchrony this morning beat with better NCOs and still slipped about 2.3% premarket on reserve cadence and costs. The reaction is therefore near a coin flip: p_up 51 on abs 4.4 gives +0.09. The findings sum is +0.10, so the two measurements agree.
bar: Disputed. Q3 2026 adjusted EPS consensus is $5.29 (TickerLeague, 10 analysts, https://tickerleague.com/companies/COF/estimates), $5.32-5.49 (Benzinga, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/COF/earnings-forecasts) or $5.43 (Zacks); GAAP EPS $4.52, revenue $16.30B, NIM 8.36%, efficiency 53.8% and an internally inconsistent 'NCO 4.63%' (Hudson Labs, 2026-10-05, https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/capital-one-q3-2026-earnings-preview-cof-results-preview). There is no company guide for EPS. Every finding is capped small for that reason.
positioning_check: Short interest is low: about 1.9% of float and 2.3 days to cover (Equibles COF page dated 2026-07-23, https://equibles.com/stocks/COF), and 8.22M shares / 1.92 days at the 2026-04-30 settlement (https://equibles.com/stocks/cof/shortinterest). No October settlement was found and the short is not crowded. Baseline 25d skew is -0.16 vol points (balanced), put/call OI 0.76, event implied move 4.36%, 20d run-up +0.72%, 5d +1.98%, and the stock is 21.7% below its 52-week high. The options market makes no directional statement.

findings.finding: Domestic card net charge-offs, already filed for two of the three Q3 months: July 4.12% and August 4.16%, against a Q2 quarterly rate of 4.71% (April 4.94, May 4.82, June 4.37; the monthly average reproduces the quarter exactly) and August 2025 at 4.70%. Card 30+ delinquency is 3.57% in August against 3.73% a year earlier. Q3 domestic card NCO is therefore tracking about 4.1-4.2%, roughly 50-60bp better quarter on quarter and year on year, and below Hudson Labs' listed 4.63% consensus NCO if that figure refers to domestic card. This implies a lower provision and room for another reserve release after Q2's $662M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 card NCO improved 39bp q/q with a $662M reserve release and adjusted EPS of $5.81 beat, yet the stock fell 2.36% on the print. Credit improvement has not been rewarded on the last three prints (-2.36, -1.52, -7.56).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the monthly 8-Ks are public and the sell side models them. The unpriced part is narrow. If the 4.63% consensus NCO is stale, provision consensus is too high and EPS consensus too low. If the market had fully priced a ~4.1% NCO quarter, adjusted EPS consensus would sit nearer Q2's $5.81 than $5.29-5.49.
findings.independence: The COMET trust September 10-D (separate document, prime seasoned pool) shows the same y/y improvement: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/922869/000116332126000029/exhibit9912002-ccseptember.htm. July figures come from a separate 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000927628/000092762826000093/ex991july2026creditmetrics.htm

findings.finding: September card credit in the Capital One Multi-asset Execution Trust 10-D, filed 2026-10-15, is the only public September read before tonight because COF files quarter-end-month metrics with earnings. Trust net charge-offs were 1.69% annualized, against 2.01% in August 2026 and 2.21% in September 2025. 30+ delinquency was 1.72%, against 1.86% a year earlier and 1.64% in August (the seasonal rise). The y/y improvement in card losses therefore held into the quarter's last month.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same line as the monthly credit metrics. COF has not rallied on improving credit in 2026 (Q2 -2.36% with an improving NCO).
findings.why_not_priced: ABS trust 10-Ds are read by credit desks, not equity previews, and none of the previews found cite a September figure. If equity holders had absorbed it, previews would quote a September NCO and the 4.63% NCO consensus would have moved toward 4.1%. It is a proxy: the trust is a seasoned, more prime pool at less than a tenth of the card book, so it shows direction, not the level.
findings.independence: Company 8-Ks for July and August (separate documents) show the same direction: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000927628/000092762826000132/ex991august2026creditmetri.htm. September 2025 comparison: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/922869/000116332125000030/exhibit9912002-ccseptember.htm

findings.finding: Synchrony, the closest card peer, reported Q3 2026 this morning (2026-10-20). EPS was $2.68 against $2.42 consensus, NCO 4.79% against 5.43% in Q2, and FY EPS guidance moved to the top of its range at ~$9.50. But 30+ delinquency rose to 4.34% from 4.16% q/q, it took a $30M reserve build against a $152M release a year earlier, and it guided a smaller-than-usual Q4 seasonal coverage decline. Shares fell 2.29% premarket, to $72.54 from $74.24, on costs, deposit betas and reserve cadence. The read-through is that a card credit beat is expected and the reaction turns on reserves and expenses.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: COF fell on its last three prints, including Q2 2026 (-2.36%) after an adjusted-EPS beat, and fell 7.56% on Q4 2025 when expenses rose 53% y/y and a reserve build replaced a release.
findings.why_not_priced: It landed this morning, after every COF preview was written. COF's spot of $202 at noon ET and its +2% five-day run-up do not suggest the market has marked COF down for the same reserve-cadence risk. If it had, COF's skew would lean to puts rather than reading -0.16.
findings.independence: Same-day headline summary (gurufocus) reports the beat: https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9131505/synchrony-financial-syf-q3-earnings-beat-boosted-by-consumer-spending. The 'shares slip' reading rests on the investing.com piece alone.

findings.finding: JPMorgan's Q3 2026 (2026-10-13) showed benign consumer card credit. Firmwide NCOs were $2.2B, down $389M y/y, and Card Services NCO was reported at 2.91% against 3.34% in Q2 and 3.15% a year earlier, with full-year card NCO guidance held at ~3.2%. JPM still took a $539M net reserve build. The read is that prime card losses are improving across the industry, while reserve releases are not automatic.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Peer credit reads have not translated into COF print-day gains in 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it is a week old and widely read. Its only incremental value is confirming the y/y card NCO improvement across a different, prime book. The 2.91% card figure comes from a secondary, undated page (https://www.nordinvestimentos.com.br/blog/jpm-resultado-3t26/) and is not verified against JPM's supplement.
findings.independence: Proxy for COF. Points the same way as COF's own monthly metrics (separate document).

findings.finding: Ally Financial's 3Q 2026 preliminary earnings review, filed today, shows GAAP EPS of $1.30 against $1.18 in both 2Q26 and 3Q25, and adjusted EPS of $1.34 against $1.21 and $1.15. This is a modest positive read on subprime/near-prime auto, about 15% of COF's loans. The retail auto NCO table could not be read from the extracted exhibit.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Auto has not been the line COF trades on. No reaction history isolates it.
findings.why_not_priced: Same-day release and a small segment for COF. The EPS beat versus consensus was not established here.

findings.finding: COF's own auto credit is drifting worse y/y while card improves. Auto NCO was 1.66% in August 2026 against 1.58% in August 2025 (July 1.48%), and the Q2 call said auto NCO rose 18bp y/y as subprime mix returns toward pre-pandemic levels. Auto 30+ delinquency is better y/y (4.54% against 5.03%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Auto is a secondary line. No isolated reaction history.
findings.why_not_priced: Public monthly data that management already flagged, so it is largely priced. It is filed so the card finding is read net of the rest of consumer credit.
findings.independence: Shares the August 8-K with the card NCO finding. Q2 call summary: https://vectorshift.ai/research/companies/capital-one-financial/earnings/2026-q2

findings.finding: Expense pressure is guided in. The Q2 call said marketing is seasonally higher in H2 than H1 (Q2 marketing ~$1.7B, +23% y/y), Brex-related marketing is still mostly ahead, and tech, AI and network investment continues. Only about a third of the $1.5B Discover expense synergies are in the run rate. Consensus efficiency of 53.8% against 57.05% in Q2 assumes a large sequential improvement.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Expenses drove the worst recent print: Q4 2025 non-interest expense +53% y/y and marketing +38% q/q, stock -7.56% (that day also carried the Brex announcement). Q2 2026 non-interest expense +7% q/q, stock -2.36%.
findings.why_not_priced: It sits inside what management guided, so it is mostly expected. The unpriced part is whether the 53.8% efficiency consensus (Hudson Labs, 2026-10-05) is too optimistic given H2 marketing seasonality. If the street had fully priced H2 marketing, consensus efficiency would not sit 3 points below Q2.
findings.independence: Hudson Labs preview, a separate document, reports management saying marketing and tech 'will remain elevated': https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/capital-one-q3-2026-earnings-preview-cof-results-preview

findings.finding: NIM is guided up for Q3. The Q2 call pointed to a catch-up as average cash falls toward the lower ending cash balance (ending cash down ~$22B to ~$55B) plus ~9bp from the extra day. Consensus NIM is 8.36% against Q2's 8.01%, so the street already has a ~35bp step-up and the risk runs both ways.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 NIM rose 14bp to 8.01% while revenue came in slightly below consensus, and the stock fell 2.36%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is inside guidance, so priced. It is filed because a NIM short of a consensus that has already embedded the full catch-up is the likeliest revenue miss.
findings.independence: Consensus NIM figure from Hudson Labs (separate document): https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/capital-one-q3-2026-earnings-preview-cof-results-preview

findings.finding: Capital headroom and buyback capacity are ample. CET1 was 13.7% at June 30 against an 11% stated long-run need and a 9.0% regulatory minimum (SCB frozen at 4.5% to 2027-09-30). The company repurchased $2.7B in Q2 and $5.2B in H1, and $11.6B remained under the $16B program at end-March, so about $8.9B was left at June 30 (my arithmetic). Investors are looking for a pace signal.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The $16B authorization came with Q3 2025 results (+1.53% that print).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. Management said it is 'not in a race'. Only a visibly faster Q3 pace (> $3B) would be news, and nothing found indicates one.

findings.finding: Financing: on 2026-09-15 COF closed EUR 1.5B of fixed-to-floating senior notes (EUR 750M 4.326% due 2032, EUR 750M 4.832% due 2037). What it buys: routine wholesale funding diversification for a deposit-funded bank with CET1 at 13.7%. There is no sign of stress, so it is signed zero.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None. COF issues senior debt regularly.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and immaterial. Filed for completeness.

findings.finding: The Discover integration is on its guided path, and the next back-book wave fell inside the window. Discover cardholders (e.g. Discover it Student) moved to Capital One's site and app on 2026-10-19, the October wave of the July/October/January conversion. Management guided the 'bottom of the brownout' in Discover loans around Q4 2026, so Q3 still carries Discover card loan contraction. The call tonight is the first comment on the October wave. No outage reports were found.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Integration commentary has framed recent prints (Q1 2026 miss, Q4 2025 costs), and the stock fell on both.
findings.why_not_priced: The schedule is guided and public. Its value tonight depends on unknown commentary (loan growth inflection timing), so it is sized at zero with a symmetric range.
findings.independence: Q2 call summary on waves and the brownout bottom (separate document): https://vectorshift.ai/research/companies/capital-one-financial/earnings/2026-q2

baseline_tension: Balanced skew (-0.16) and a flat 20-day run-up give the market no lean. My evidence is a public-data credit beat offset by a reaction function that has sold COF's last three prints and by Synchrony slipping on a beat this morning, so it neither agrees with nor cuts against the baseline. p_up stays at 51.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): COF sold its Q2 beat and its last three prints, so the July/August card NCO finding went from +0.6 to +0.4 and the September trust finding from +0.4 to +0.3; p_up went from 52 to 51.

Rule 6 (verify the bar): the EPS bar is disputed ($5.29-5.49 adjusted, $4.52 GAAP, an inconsistent 4.63% NCO), so every finding stays capped small. The drafts were already under 1 point and nothing else moved.
Rule 5 (proxies smaller than company series): the COMET trust, JPM and Ally reads were already sized below the company 8-K finding. Left standing.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): the EUR 1.5B notes are routine funding with a CET1 of 13.7%. Kept at zero.
Rule 7 (positioning): short interest is about 1.9% of float and 2.3 days to cover, not crowded, so the negatives were not shrunk for squeeze risk.
